confirmedRules.name: Keyboard shortcuts for copy, paste, undo, redo and delete
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Ctrl or Cmd plus C copies the selected object, V pastes a clone and clears the redo history, Z undoes and Y redoes. Delete or Backspace removes the selected object unless it is a text being edited.
confirmedRules.given: The document has keyboard focus and an object is selected (not in text-editing mode)
confirmedRules.when: The user presses Ctrl/Cmd+C, Ctrl/Cmd+V, Ctrl/Cmd+Z, Ctrl/Cmd+Y, or BACKSPACE/DEL
confirmedRules.then: C stores the active object as the copy target. V clones it (or every member of a multi-selection), selects the clones and empties the redo stack. Z/Y run undo/redo and discard any 'stack empty' errors without a message. DEL/BACKSPACE prevents the browser default and removes the active object
confirmedRules.parameters: Key codes come from consts.keyCodes (C, V, Z, Y, BACKSPACE, DEL); modifier = ctrlKey OR metaKey
edgeCases: Paste without a previous copy resolves to an empty result (graphics pasteObject, line 16135)
A pasted clone becomes the new copy target, so pressing paste again clones the clone
Removal is blocked while a text object isEditing (graphics isReadyRemoveObject, line 14900-14903)
A multi-selection is wrapped in a new fabric Group and that group is removed as one undoable command (graphics line 14880-14892)
The listener is attached to the whole document, so the shortcuts also fire when focus is in other inputs on the page
confirmedRules.suspectedDefect: The paste clears the redo stack but does not record its own undo command here. Copy and paste are not undoable at this level unless the graphics layer fires addObject. Also, a document-wide keydown can delete canvas objects while the user types Backspace in an unrelated form field if a canvas object is still active.

confirmedRules.name: Undoable vs silent command execution
confirmedRules.plainEnglish: Every editing operation goes through a command invoker that records it on the undo stack. Silent execution applies the change without recording history. Undo and redo replay that history.
confirmedRules.given: An edit such as addShape, applyFilter, flip or rotate (non-silent)
confirmedRules.then: The invoker runs the command with the Graphics instance injected as the first argument and pushes it onto the undo stack. Undo/redo stack-length changes are re-emitted as undoStackChanged/redoStackChanged events (lines 1061-1088)
confirmedRules.parameters: Silent path: executeSilent (used by rotate/setAngle when isSilent=true, and by setObjectPropertiesQuietly which bypasses the invoker entirely)
edgeCases: Objects created interactively on the canvas (addObject event) get an ADD_OBJECT command pushed directly onto the undo stack without re-executing it (lines 1282-1286, 2119-2123)
Changing text in place fires textChanged, which runs a CHANGE_TEXT command so the edit is undoable (lines 2034-2037)
clearUndoStack/clearRedoStack/isEmpty* expose the stack state (lines 2521-2557)
confirmedRules.smeQuestion: P0 panel split on whether this is critical to the system's core purpose or a costly-if-wrong rule (The rule card matches the code. Lines 1428-1462 add the Graphics instance as the first argument and pass the call to the invoker's execute or executeSilent. The invoker code outside the cited range confirms the rest. Around line 4562, _invokeExecution only pushes to the undo stack when _isSilent is false. Around line 4652, executeSilent sets _isSilent before running the command. Around line 2646, setObjectPropertiesQuietly calls graphics.setObjectProperties directly and skips the invoker. Around line 1729, rotate uses executeSilent when the silent flag is set. Lines 1061-1088 re-emit undoStackChanged and redoStackChanged. Two small gaps in the card: it does not mention that silent execution still clears the redo stack, or that the invoker lock rejects a command while another one is running. Neither changes the substance. Through the compliance lens, this is not P0. It is the undo/redo history of a browser image editor. It moves no money and enforces no legal requirement. It is not an audit trail, because it lives only in memory, is lost when the session ends, and is meant to be undone. If it changed silently, a regulator, auditor or finance controller would not care. A broken undo is a usability problem, not a costly or permanent one, and undo/redo is a supporting feature rather than the central job the editor exists to do. It should be P1 or P2, checked with ordinary regression tests. No instruction-like text appears in the cited lines. | Faithful. ImageEditor.execute (dist/tui-image-editor.js:1428-1445) puts this._graphics first in the args and calls Invoker.execute. Invoker._invokeExecution (4550-4575) then pushes the command onto the undo stack after it succeeds, unless _isSilent is set. executeSilent (1451-1462 -> 4651-4663) sets _isSilent=true and resets it once the command finishes. rotate and setAngle only take the silent path when isSilent is true (1726-1780). setObjectPropertiesQuietly (2645-2648) calls _graphics.setObjectProperties directly and skips the invoker. Undo and redo go straight to the invoker (1471-1487). _attachInvokerEvents (1061-1088) re-fires UNDO_STACK_CHANGED and REDO_STACK_CHANGED. The card leaves out some behavior that matters for an equivalence contract: (1) every execute, silent ones included, clears the redo stack (4693-4694), so a silent rotate still wipes redo history. (2) While a command is running the invoker is locked: a second execute is rejected with isLock (4680-4682), and an undo during that time puts the command back on the stack without running it (4710-4713). (3) A command is only pushed to the undo stack if it succeeds; a rejected command is not recorded. These gaps make the card incomplete but not wrong. On priority, it does not justify P0. This is generic undo/redo plumbing in an image editor (the vendored TOAST UI pattern). It is a usability feature, not the editor's core calculation or decision. It does not move money or guard security, regulatory or irreversible data. A wrong undo stack can be recovered and is visible to the user. P1 is more appropriate. No instruction-shaped text in the cited lines. The Spanish comment at 12227 only documents the meaning of isSilent.) — confirm criticality.

All temporary steps are removed from undo history afterwards.

On success the command is pushed to the undo stack and the redo stack is cleared (execute 4693-4695 calls clearRedoStack; _invokeExecution 4562-4564 calls pushUndoStack). On failure nothing is pushed, the lock is released and the rejection is passed on (4571-4574). The basic claim holds. On success the command is pushed onto the undo stack and undoStackChanged fires with the new length. The redo stack is then cleared, and redoStackChanged fires with 0, but only if the redo stack was not already empty. On failure nothing is pushed, the lock is released, the rejection is passed on and the redo stack is left alone.

The order in the Then step is wrong. The card says the redo stack is cleared and then executeCallback runs. The code does it the other way round. _invokeExecution pushes to the undo stack, unlocks, and calls command.executeCallback(value) right away (4563-4568). clearRedoStack only runs later, in the .then that execute attaches (4693-4694). rejectedRules.rejectionReason: refuted: The cited lines are a theme config object, and most of the rule's values do appear there: 'common.bi.image' = img/LogoDoble.png (black-theme.js:4), 'common.bisize.height' = 77px (:7), 'common.backgroundColor' = #1e1e1e (:9). Lines 26 and 33 (download button #fdba3b, canvasTamano #336BFF) fall outside the cited range but also match. index.html:271 does pass theme: blackTheme. The rule's central claim is still false: it says the header shows both LogoDoble.png and LogoCanarias.png. The key 'common.bi.imageC' (black-theme.js:5) is never read. The theme resolver handles 'common.bi' and returns only styles[type].image (dist/tui-image-editor.js:6793-6794). The header template emits a single (dist/tui-image-editor.js:6520, and again at 6655). No code anywhere in legacy/tonga/dist/tui-image-editor.js reads 'imageC'. So only LogoDoble.png is drawn, and the LogoCanarias.png entry is dead configuration. The comment at black-theme.js:2 ('Meto el logo único', i.e. 'I add the single logo') agrees with this. A corrected rule would read: the header shows only img/LogoDoble.png, sized by common.bisize.height 77px, on a #1e1e1e background. No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited region.
